executor_boundary_proof.connection_used: django.db.connection (the real mechanism execute_approved_merge() is designed to run under)

defect.summary: compute_plan_fingerprint() is non-deterministic across this repository's two real DB connection mechanisms for jsonb-typed fingerprinted fields
defect.root_cause: Django's connection.cursor() returns jsonb columns as raw str (uncanonicalized JSON text) when used for raw SQL; a bare psycopg2.connect() connection (litrix_db.db()) auto-decodes the same column into a native dict, which _normalize_scalar() canonicalizes via json.dumps(sort_keys=True); the str branch returns the raw text unmodified, un-sorted

evidence.citations_by_year_not_visible_in_this_ca: this pair's CitationsByYear keys (2022-2026) already happen to sort in ascending/alphabetical order, coincidentally masking the same underlying bug

why_not_caught_before: all 224 existing tests use mocked cursors that construct dict values directly in fixtures, never exercising real jsonb decoding via either connection type
every prior live canary check (12 confirmations, Phase 4G through 4O) used litrix_db.db() (raw psycopg2), which always takes the already-canonical dict branch
this phase is the first time the fingerprint was computed via Django's connection, the actual mechanism execute_approved_merge() is designed to run under
defect.safety_characterization: fail-safe, not fail-open -- causes a spurious STALE_FINGERPRINT block on unchanged data, never an incorrect ALLOW
defect.recommended_fix: make _normalize_scalar() attempt json.loads() on a str input before its existing dict-canonicalization path, falling back to current string handling only if parsing fails
defect.fix_applied_this_phase_reason: explicit instruction: do not modify executor/dedup logic without a proven defect and even then prefer a separate, dedicated phase, matching this project's established audit-then-fix discipline (e.g. Phase 4K -> 4K.1)

can_valid_approved_approval_be_created.evidence: ApprovalID=1, live in production, Status=APPROVED, correct direction, real reviewer, correct AuditLog cross-reference

path_to_merge_without_valid_approval.note: the defect found causes spurious blocking of a legitimate approval, not a bypass

fingerprint_binding_actually_works.note: the binding/scoping/mismatch-rejection logic is proven correct; the fingerprint value it binds to is not yet deterministic across this repo's two real connection mechanisms

conflicting_or_orphaned_records.note: exactly one row, correct identity, correct state, no duplicates, no strays

cleanup_decision.decision: keep the real APPROVED approval as-is; do not revoke, do not delete
reasoning: the approval workflow itself has zero defects -- the human decision it represents remains valid
verdict A (READY FOR FIRST CONTROLLED CANARY MERGE) presupposes a real, unrevoked APPROVED approval surviving this phase
the fingerprint defect affects only whether the executor can currently validate against it, not whether the approval decision itself is sound
matches this project's established practice of not deleting approval history when the design intends to keep it (Phase 4H/4K.1)
